origins: Being left out, teased, or ignored, especially in childhood or adolescence, can plant the idea that we are unlikable. A few painful experiences can become a lens: a friend who does not text back means dislike, a quiet group means rejection. The belief then shapes behavior. We withdraw, wait to be chosen, or expect the worst, and that can reduce the connection we long for.
teaches: Jesus said to His disciples, “I have called you friends.” Scripture says, “There is a friend who stays closer than a brother,” and “A friend loves at all times.” God’s thoughts toward you are personal: “How precious to me are Your thoughts, O God, how vast is their sum!” and “The LORD your God is among you… He will rejoice over you with singing.” If the Creator delights in you, then you are not unlikable. Friendship takes time and risk, but the starting point is that you are already known and wanted by God.
self_statements: If I disappeared, nobody would notice.
Everyone finds me boring or annoying.
They are being nice out of pity.
I will always be on the outside.
There is something unlikable about me.
errors: Assuming I know what others think of me.
Treating a few rejections as proof that nobody likes me.
Feeling disliked and concluding that I am.
questions: What evidence do I have that someone likes me, even a little?
Who has been kind to me or reached out?
Where did I learn that I am unlikable?
Am I rejecting people before they can reject me?
What does God say about how He sees me?
What is one small step toward connection I could take?
truth: I am not unlikable. Jesus calls me His friend, and God rejoices over me. Some people may not connect with me, but that is not a verdict on my worth. I can take small, steady steps toward friendship.
hw_truths: God rejoices over me with singing.
A few rejections do not define me.
I can take a step toward others.
log: Each day, write one kind word, text, or smile you received or gave.
actions: Write names of people who have been kind or interested in you.
Send one message or invite one person for coffee.
Write the thought “they will reject me” and test it afterward.
Let it remind you who calls you friend.
prayer: Lord Jesus, You call me friend. Heal the places where I have been rejected. Give me courage to reach out and eyes to see the people who care about me. Amen.
hw_questions: Who has been kind to me?
What evidence do I have that someone likes me?
Where did I learn I am unlikable?
What does God say about me?
What small step can I take?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Jesus has called me His friend, so I am not unlikable.”
